scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FIX.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a response-handling problem (SH-CS framing): tickets pile up because responses are slow or templated, and an AI auto-answer/auto-fix agent would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (e.g. read-type handling or tariff logic) around August introduced systematic bill errors driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: AMI read delivery from the vendor (MDMS) to billing is failing or delivering invalid reads, forcing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads are not being completed or delivered, causing missing reads and estimate substitution that overstate bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-OVERUS.statement: The estimate-substitution logic itself (used whenever no accepted read is available) is flawed or triggered too often, producing inaccurate bills regardless of which upstream source failed.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry an ACTUAL read, implying a billing-side error in processing/calculating bills from accepted actual reads, separate from any estimate-substitution path.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field-reader staffing shortfall (three readers short since July, per SH-FIELD) causes late manual-read routes, forcing estimate substitution for the affected customer subset.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db's tariff_change_log contains zero records, meaning no tariff rate/logic changes were made in the queried window. This rules out a tariff-logic change as the cause of bill errors but says nothing about read-type handling rules, which live in a separate log (DA-RULES/billing-config) not yet queried.

Of all disputed bills, 1240 are tied to ESTIMATED reads and 1785 to ACTUAL reads — i.e. the majority (about 59%) of disputed bills involved an actual meter read, not an estimate. This means estimate-substitution-driven causes (AMI export failure, field read failure, estimate-logic flaw) can at most account for the ESTIMATED-read subset and cannot explain the larger ACTUAL-read portion of the dispute surge.

crm-tickets dispute_response_times shows 2440 tickets with median response of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both within the 3.0-day SLA; response handling speed is not lagging. This undercuts the premise that slow/templated responses are driving the dispute surge, independent of the separate read-type findings (E-01, E-02) about bill accuracy.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year, which corroborates E-01's authoritative tariff_change_log finding of zero records for the Aug-Sep window.

route-log shows manual field-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for Aug-Sep, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. a real completion shortfall exists in the contracted field-reading process during the dispute-surge window.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager, an interested party seeking contract headcount increase) claims the field-reading contractor has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a specific causal mechanism behind the completion shortfall already observed in E-05 (0.88 vs 0.95 target), but SH-FIELD's stated incentive and potential bias toward attributing problems to staffing mean it should not be treated as confirmed.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes at 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul), then jumping to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep). This confirms the initial request's framing that volume roughly doubled starting in August, and shows the surge persisted and slightly worsened into September rather than being a one-month blip.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document confirms a contractual authorization process (service contract §4.2): the utility can request field route priority changes, but execution is conditioned on Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation. It corroborates the already-modeled K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update and says nothing about the causes of the dispute surge.

U-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUSE.question: What specific billing import validation rule or calculation logic (e.g. read-type handling) changed around August to cause incorrect bills from accepted actual reads?
U-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any concrete bill-correction path exists; without it SC-ROOT-CAUSE cannot be met and no remediation design (automated or manual) is justified.
U-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query DA-RULES via billing-config for rule changes around August 2026 and correlate their timing/affected accounts with E-02's ACTUAL-read disputed bills.
U-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Ship only diagnostic scope (investigate_billing_rule_change, analyze_disputed_bills_by_read_type); defer any bill-correction action until the specific defect is identified and confirmed by Billing Operations.

U-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDITY.question: Is the field-reader staffing shortfall (E-06, SH-FIELD claim) the actual cause of the route completion shortfall (E-05), or are other factors (route design, equipment) responsible?
U-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether route-completion remediation should target staffing versus other causes, and whether SH-FIELD's incentive-biased claim should drive scope.
U-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log route assignment/completion records against ORG-FIELD operational records beyond SH-FIELD's statement.
U-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat the route completion shortfall (E-05) as the operative metric and do not assume staffing is the cause when scoping remediation.

U-AMI-EXPORT-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does AMI read delivery from the MDMS vendor to billing have failures or invalid reads contributing to the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset?
U-AMI-EXPORT-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Would identify an additional upstream cause for the ESTIMATED-read dispute stream beyond the route completion shortfall already observed.
U-AMI-EXPORT-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Once Telemetrix (ORG-AMI) provisions mdms-export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING/DEGRADED, no fallback), query AMI read events for the ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts.
U-AMI-EXPORT-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db and route-log analysis only; treat query_ami_read_events as non-blocking pending vendor access and exclude AMI-export causes from the confirmed causal chain until resolved.

U-DISPUTE-COUNT-AS-SUCCESS-SIG.question: Does a drop in monthly dispute ticket count reliably indicate bills are now correct, or could ticket volume fall for other reasons (e.g. a changed CS intake/response policy) while billing errors persist?
U-DISPUTE-COUNT-AS-SUCCESS-SIG.decision_impact: Affects whether M-DISPUTE-VOL alone is a valid success signal or must be paired with a bill-accuracy metric.
U-DISPUTE-COUNT-AS-SUCCESS-SIG.resolution_path: Review CRM intake/response policy changes alongside dispute volume trend to confirm a drop reflects fewer billing errors rather than a changed intake process.
U-DISPUTE-COUNT-AS-SUCCESS-SIG.safe_placeholder: Pair M-DISPUTE-VOL with M-ACTUAL-READ-SHARE / billing-db accuracy checks rather than relying on ticket count alone as the success signal.

U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-FIELD-BILL manual meter read handoff from ORG-FIELD to ORG-UTIL delivering complete and semantically valid reads (delivery_status and semantic_validity both UNKNOWN)?
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff is dropping or corrupting reads, the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset and the route completion metric (E-05) could be inflated by delivery failure rather than genuine route/staffing shortfall.
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Reconcile route-log completed-route counts against billing-db accepted-read counts for the same period to confirm the handoff's delivery and semantic validity.
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat E-05's 0.88 completion figure as provisional and do not attribute the ESTIMATED-read dispute stream solely to staffing until the handoff is confirmed reliable.

U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-MDMS-BILL nightly AMI export handoff from ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL delivering complete and semantically valid reads (delivery_status and semantic_validity both UNKNOWN)?
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff fails or delivers invalid reads, MDMS data could already be contaminated before query_ami_read_events analysis, confounding the AMI-export-contribution question.
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Once mdms-export access is provisioned, check MDMS export logs/timestamps against billing-db import timestamps for gaps or malformed records.
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Do not use MDMS AMI data to confirm or refute billing-side causes until handoff validity is confirmed; rely on already-committed billing-db/route-log/CRM evidence (E-01 to E-07).

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director, the requester) asked for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Monthly dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600 (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260 (Aug-Sep) and remained elevated into September (E-07).
Majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are tied to an ACTUAL meter read rather than ESTIMATED (E-02).
Manual field-read route completion is below the contracted target (0.88 vs 0.95, E-05).
Dispute response times are already within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA, E-03), so slow responses are not the symptom's driver.
problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) and the surge persists (E-07). A secondary, smaller stream of disputes (1240 bills) is tied to ESTIMATED reads, consistent with a field route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-05).
